segments.text: SPEAKER 1: Good afternoon, everyone.
I'm here for Ludo Robotics.
Ludo Robotics is a startup building AI
for social intelligent robot.
And I'll explain what that means in a minute.
We are a research team based in Palo Alto and Seoul.
We have built many amazing things in the past,
including PUBG, one of the most successful video games
in the history.
PUBGALLY is the first AI agent that
plays games with players with voice communication.
Raon is the state of the art speech language
models of the same size, and also
many interesting technology behind coding agents
such as Meta-Harness and Terminus-KIRA.
So what do I mean by socially intelligent robot?
Robots could be smart in two different ways-- physically
smart, socially smart.
Right now we don't have either.
A physically smart but socially dumb
robot will be useful in factories, mostly
in cages setup.
They'll do really great work at factories.
But imagine the other way around.
What if we take the current robot
with the current level of physical capacity
and give them really good social intelligence?
What can we do that?
They can walk around well, they can carry things around.
Now if they can talk to people, they
can understand people and the society,
they can probably start doing something very amazing.
Imagine that a humanoid who can walk their dogs
or who can pick your kids carrying their heavy bags
and having some fun conversation walking back.
So even with the current level of physical capacity,
by giving them a social intelligence,
we can enable much more interesting things.
Of course, in the end, we all want
to be at the right upper corner where the robots are all
smart in both ways.
However, if you have to take a path,
Ludo Robotics decided to take the other path
than the other path that people are using.
We are focusing on improving the social intelligence
with the current robots, and with that vision, introducing
Ludi 0.1.
So this is our first research product.
It's an agentic system for improving
the social intelligence of the current robot.
As you can see, it's controlled by a vision language model.
It's a $4 billion local model controlling all different tools.
VLM takes care of the perception, reasoning
and decides which tool to use.
VLA is an action tool.
So if you call on VLA, the robot will use their body.
You can use navigation speech tools to talk to the people.
So without further ado, I will show you a few video
demos taken in our lab.
So in this demo, you will see two people using
the robot in different ways.
